thread:
alex: Heads-up — getting a customer escalation: sustained 502s from edge for hosted-api in eu-west, started ~12:22 UTC. Sample request-id: req_3f9a2c. Customer says it spikes on streaming calls and large payloads.

jordan: on it. are these single-tenant or guest calls? any auth rotation around that time?

alex: mostly guest/anonymous keys. not seeing a global auth rotation in control plane. quick curl that repros for me:

alex: ```
curl -v https://api-eu.redwood.ai/v1/stream 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer guest_xxx' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  --data '{"model":"x","input":"lot of text..."}' 
  --http2
```

ingress-bot: alert: edge-proxy eu-west: 502-rate +420% in 5m, p95 latency upstream 430ms, h2 keepalive pool exhaustion flagged. top upstream: midproxy-frontend-2. metrics: https://internal/alerts/5902

maria: looking at frontdoor traces — I see a common pattern: long-lived h2 streams where upstream closes the stream and envoy returns 502. conn window shows many streams in `half-closed (local)` state and h2 slot exhaustion. correlated with auth-cache churn on a few tenants.

alex: trace ids: 3f9a2c, 3f9a9e, 3f9b10. also noticed errors concentrated for requests with chunked streaming and large metadata headers (~2.1KB). customer workaround reported: switching to non-streaming or reducing concurrent streams reduced hits.

jordan: can we try a quick canary: set `Connection: close` to break persistent h2 keepalives and see if rate drops? also try disabling client-side http2 for a test tenant. if that reduces 502s it'll point to keepalive/connpool exhaustion.

samir: customer said adding `Connection: close` removed errors for them. sounds like h2 keepalive pool exhaustion ejection. we should consider short-term mitigation: reduce per-tenant keepalive window + increase midproxy pool and enable L7 backoff to avoid hard 502s.

maria: agreed. I'll open an ingress config change: lower `max_keepalive_streams` for guest frontdoor from 100 -> 20 for 5 minutes and scale midproxy-frontend by +2 replicas in eu-west. oncall: can you run the change? I'll also toggle L7 backoff so Envoy will return 503/429 instead of 502 during overload.

alex: running change now — using `kubectl patch` on ingress-config and scaling deployment: 

alex: ```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap ingress-flags --patch '{"data":{"max_keepalive_streams":"20"}}'
kubectl -n infra scale deploy midproxy-frontend --replicas=6
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: ingress-flags patch by alex (runbook id 9021)
deploy-bot: deploy completed: ingress-flags patched in eu-west (duration 42s) :white_check_mark:

maria: metrics look better — 502 rate down ~85% in 3m after applying keepalive reduction + extra replicas. still watching for auth-cache churn correlation but core symptom looks like h2 connpool exhaustion on guest heavy streaming.

jordan: good catch. next steps: follow up with platform to build a safe per-tenant keepalive throttle, add an automated mitigation playbook (toggle backoff + scale), and add a probe that alerts on h2 half-closed stream counts.

samir: I'll update the customer with repro steps and the temporary mitigation. they reported Connection: close as a useful short-term fix, will advise on best practices (chunking, backpressure). :thumbsup:

maria: assign postmortem action items: 1) root cause writeup, 2) telemetry dashboard for h2 stream states, 3) grad school of ingresses to test keepalive thresholds in staging. tagging eng-sre for follow-up.

alex: thanks all, will capture traces and customer repro notes in the ticket.
